items.statement: The authors concluded that substantial socioeconomic inequalities in HRQoL occurred during the pandemic, with the largest disparities in the UK and work status as the strongest and most consistent SES predictor.
source: Full article, Abstract > Conclusions

items.statement: The authors interpreted LSS and EQ VAS as identifying similar key determinants, while EQ VAS appeared more responsive to income- and education-related differences.
source: Full article, Discussion, paragraphs beginning “In our study we used both” and “In contrast”

items.statement: The cross-sectional design does not establish temporal order and does not support causal inference; reverse causality is possible.
source: Full article, Strengths and Limitations, first paragraph

items.statement: Exclusion of approximately 10% of respondents with missing income can bias income-related estimates because non-response can relate to demographic and health characteristics.
source: Full article, Strengths and Limitations, second paragraph

items.statement: Online panel recruitment can cause selection bias and underrepresent older adults and people with limited internet access or lower literacy.
source: Full article, Strengths and Limitations, third paragraph

items.statement: The binary work-status variable combined employment, study, retirement, caregiving, inability to work, and unemployment in ways that can hide important distinctions and reduce cross-country comparability.
source: Full article, Strengths and Limitations, fourth paragraph

items.statement: Use of LSS instead of country-specific utility values limits comparison with utility studies and integration into economic evaluation.
source: Full article, Strengths and Limitations, fifth paragraph

items.statement: Cultural differences in self-reporting EQ-5D-5L and EQ VAS can influence the outcomes.
source: Full article, Strengths and Limitations, sixth paragraph

items.statement: Pandemic conditions, absence of pre-pandemic data, and unmodeled national institutional factors limit temporal and cross-country interpretation.
source: Full article, Strengths and Limitations, first and final paragraphs

items.statement: The large number of tests can increase Type I error, and the study did not apply a formal multiple-testing correction.
source: Full article, Methods > Statistical analysis, penultimate paragraph

items.label: Valuation-free cross-country HRQoL comparison
items.description: The authors selected LSS because it uses reported severity levels without country-specific value sets, which differ in elicitation methods and can introduce structural heterogeneity.
